ideas.title: Environment Agency waste carriers, brokers and dealers register (England) on gankdat: lookups + new/expiring/lapsed change feed
ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-05 (burn-down starvation fallback). Supply: the EA electronic Public Register serves the register as an API without registration under the Environment Agency Conditional Licence (api.gov.uk/ea/public-registers-for-environmental-information; data.gov.uk dataset 961d75f3), upper-tier registrations renew every 3 years so expiry is a natural change feed. Demand: two Apify actors already price it — devon_gtme/uk-waste-carriers-register from $2 per 1k results (new/expiring/lapsed tracking, CBDU search) and nerolabs/uk-waste-carrier-monitor at $0.01 per record, $0.05 per detected change — and wastecheck.co.uk sells a real-time carrier-verification API with a free tier; the buyer is the construction, facilities and waste-broker compliance team doing the legal duty-of-care check on every contractor. Same DataSource shape as uk-gambling-operators (register in D1 with idOf on the CBDU number, daily wave). Score ≈ 4: evidence 2 (paid actors and an API vendor, no price above $0.05) × reach 2 (our Apify, MCP and x402 shelves) ÷ 1 build day; owner minutes 0. Parked because STRATEGY §5 puts distribution before new datasets until a shelf converts, and two caveats need the relay first: the Conditional Licence text (commercial reuse and attribution terms, not plain OGL) and the 2026-10-01 EA blog moving registration to GOV.UK, which may change the register endpoint. Exchange 2026-W41: the two Apify actors it cited sit at 2 users each (relay store read) — evidence down to 1.
ideas.trigger: a gankdat shelf converts (≥ 1 paying account or ≥ 20 paid Apify runs/month) or the 2026-10-30 funnel review shows KYB/compliance lookups; then relay-read the Conditional Licence and the register API before scoring for the queue

ideas.title: HM Land Registry Price Paid Data (England & Wales sold house prices) on gankdat: postcode/street lookups + monthly new-sales feed
ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-07 (burn-down starvation fallback). Supply: HM Land Registry publishes every registered residential sale since 1995 as CSV under the Open Government Licence v3.0, commercial use allowed, with the fixed attribution line ("Contains HM Land Registry data © Crown copyright and database right <year>. This data is licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0"); a monthly update file plus yearly files of 115–230 MB (gov.uk price-paid-data-downloads), no registration, no personal names in the rows, so no Blind Mode work. Demand: nine Apify actors already sell exactly this — alinz/uk-sold-house-prices and logiover/uk-land-registry-scraper from $1.50 per 1k, devon_gtme/land-registry-price-paid and kaz_kakyo/uk-property-data $2, bgfc97 $3, scrapers_lat $6.80, plotbench $10 — and propertydata.co.uk sells the same rows inside a £28–£576/month API. The buyer is the proptech, surveyor and lettings tool pulling comparables by postcode. Score ≈ 3: evidence 3 (nine priced rivals, a £28/month API) × reach 2 (Apify, MCP, x402) ÷ 2 build days (the full file is ~30M rows — a rolling 24-month window in D1 with idOf on the transaction id and a monthly wave, not the whole history) ÷ a crowding penalty (nine rivals at $1.50 and up means price, not scarcity, is the only lever, and every Apify category we list in sits at the 2-user floor — exchange 2026-W41). Parked: STRATEGY §5 puts distribution before new datasets until a shelf converts; apify.com and gov.uk are relay-only hosts, so the rivals' user counts and the monthly file layout were not read tonight.
ideas.trigger: a gankdat shelf converts (≥ 1 paying account or ≥ 20 paid Apify runs/month) and a relay store read shows ≥ 2 of the nine rivals above 10 users/30 d; then relay-read the monthly update file header and size before scoring for the queue

ideas.title: ICO register of fee payers (1.4M UK data controllers) on gankdat: registration lookup + expiry/new-registration feeds
ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-08 (burn-down starvation fallback), read through the relay (docs/relay/responses/ico-fee-payers, pruned after 7 days). Supply: the ICO publishes the whole register as one daily zip, register-of-data-controllers-YYYY-MM-DD.zip (77,487,958 bytes on 2026-10-08, SHA256 on the page, served from a /media2/<hash>/ path that a wave must read off the download page rather than guess); published fields are controller name and address, registration reference, fee tier, date registered and expiry, other trading names, and DPO contact (DPO name only with consent). Licence, verbatim from the download page: "the dataset is available for re-use under the Open Government Licence, the licence does not apply to personal data in the dataset" — so sole-trader entries and DPO names are personal data and go through Blind Mode (drop or aggregate the name, keep tier/postcode area/expiry), as uk-company-profiles does for officers; limited companies, charities and the 51,611 public authorities are organisation data. Demand: one Apify actor already sells exactly this — uksignals/ico-signals, "UK Business Data Scraper: 1.4M Organisations, Renewal Dates", from $3.00 per 1,000 organisation records, published ~2026-08-25, 2 users total, 1 in 30 days, 46 runs — and its pitch (renewal dates, size tier, postcode, trading names, public-authority filter) is the buyer: GDPR consultancies and DPO-as-a-service firms chasing registrations about to expire, and procurement tools checking a supplier is registered. No vendor was found selling a per-month ICO feed; the register's own search is free one-at-a-time. Score ≈ 2: evidence 2 (one priced rival at the 2-user floor, free official search) × reach 2 (Apify, MCP, x402) ÷ 2 build days (daily zip → D1 with idOf on the registration reference, a daily wave that diffs expiry and new rows, Blind Mode for the sole-trader share, actor + landing card) — below the distribution items STRATEGY §5 puts first. Parked: every data shelf we list on sits at the 2-user floor (exchange 2026-W41), and the one rival shows the same floor for this register.
ideas.trigger: a gankdat shelf converts (≥ 1 paying account or ≥ 20 paid Apify runs/month), or an inbound request names ICO registration / supplier due diligence; then relay-read RANGE=0-4095 of the day's zip (CSV header, encoding, sole-trader share) before scoring it for the gankdat queue

ideas.title: VOA non-domestic rating list (England & Wales business rates) on gankdat: rateable-value lookup + weekly change feed
ideas.why: Pre-research 2026-10-09 (burn-down starvation fallback), read through the relay (docs/relay/responses/voa-rating-list-2026-10-09, pruned after 7 days). Supply: the Valuation Office (part of HMRC since 2026-04-01) publishes the whole non-domestic rating list and the summary valuations for England and Wales free of charge at voaratinglists.blob.core.windows.net/html/rlidata.htm — epoch snapshots per list year (2026 epoch 0004, 2023 epoch 0023, 2017 and 2010 still maintained), weekly change-update files applied on top of the latest epoch, asterisk-delimited ASCII CSV inside zips of 2M+ rows, a blob-storage directory listing for automation, and a layout PDF (Compiled Rating List and Summary Valuation Data Specification) — exactly the shape of a weekly change feed (new assessments, deletions and rateable-value changes per billing authority) that rating agents, fit-out and energy suppliers and property investors would pay for. Licence, verbatim from the download page: "VO Rating List Downloads are only available under our restricted licence terms and conditions. These are the same terms and conditions applicable to viewing rating list information online. An open government licence does not apply." The terms (tax.service.gov.uk/business-rates-find/terms-and-conditions): "Publication of this information and its use is restricted to Non Domestic Rating (NDR) purposes only" — anyone viewing assessments, and an interested person (occupier or owner), the billing authority, their authorised representative or a firm serving them, reviewing their own and comparable valuations; "Onward disclosure to a third party is prohibited except where the third party's use is for the uses stated above"; the user "will delete this information when they no longer have a business need associated with the stated purposes"; Crown copyright and Crown database right. A gankdat dataset, MCP tool or Apify actor sold to anyone is onward disclosure for a non-NDR purpose — the same category as Land Registry CCOD/OCOD and the FCA register (STRATEGY §5). Demand exists and the one priced rival ignores the licence: Apify spookyweb/uk-business-rates, "from $0.60 / 1,000 valuations", pay-per-event, 2 users total and 1 monthly, no run count shown, resells the same list filtered by postcode, council, description code and value range (WebSearch 2026-10-09; its .md listing returns 404 through the relay). No priced change-alert service for rating surveyors was found; Analyse LOCAL (G-Cloud) sells rating-list analysis to councils on quote; HMRC's Business Rates API is a private trial for registered ratepayers. Declined on licence, not demand.
ideas.trigger: the Valuation Office moves the downloads to the Open Government Licence (the 2023 'transparency and disclosure of information on business rates valuations' consultation points that way) — then relay-read the data specification PDF and RANGE=0-4095 of the latest 2026 change-update zip and score it for the gankdat queue; or a rating agent (an authorised representative under the terms) asks for comparables for its own clients — then a private per-customer feed under their licence, never a shelf listing
